gaps.narrative: The institution lacks a formalised procedure for submitting suspicious activity reports to the Financial Intelligence Unit, creating a material gap against reporting obligations.
gaps.source_text: Obligated entities shall report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit without delay.

gaps.narrative: Customer identification records are not retained beyond three years, falling short of the mandatory five-year minimum retention period following the end of the business relationship.
gaps.source_text: Member States shall require obligated entities to retain documents and information for a minimum of five years after the end of the business relationship.

gaps.narrative: No enhanced due diligence measures are applied to customers identified as politically exposed persons, representing a significant gap in the institution's high-risk customer management framework.
gaps.source_text: Obligated entities shall apply enhanced customer due diligence measures in respect of transactions or business relationships with politically exposed persons.

gaps.narrative: The business risk assessment has not been updated in the past 24 months and does not reflect current typologies, leaving the institution without an adequate basis for calibrating its controls.
gaps.source_text: Each Member State shall take appropriate steps to identify, assess, understand and mitigate the risks of money laundering and terrorist financing affecting it.

gaps.narrative: The transaction monitoring system does not cover intra-group transfers, resulting in a blind spot for patterns of structuring activity conducted across affiliated entities.
gaps.source_text: Obligated entities shall examine, as far as reasonably possible, the background and purpose of all transactions that are complex, unusually large, or conducted in an unusual pattern.
